title: async fn returns a future
summary: Calling an async fn does nothing yet - it builds a machine that .await (or an executor) must drive.
lecture: An `async fn fetch() -> i32` does not return an i32. It returns an anonymous Future that will EVENTUALLY produce an i32 - and calling it runs none of the body. Futures are inert values: no executor, no progress.

`.await` is how one future drives another, legal only inside async contexts. At the outermost edge, an executor (tokio's runtime, or a minimal block_on loop) polls the future to completion - that's where async meets the synchronous world.

The classic symptom of a forgotten .await: a type error complaining that `impl Future<Output = i32>` isn't an i32 (or doesn't implement Display). The value you wanted is one keyword away, still wrapped in the machine that computes it.

example.caption: async builds machines; .await runs them.
